sources_note: Every external claim carries its source inline in the vault note; this file is the structured extract for the harness to consume.

existing_infra.ppm_stats: scouter/core/ppm.py: stdlib-only P6 PPM parser, 256-bin per-channel histograms (Counter over the high byte of 16-bit samples), luminance histogram (Rec.709 weights on channel counts, labelled an estimate), percentiles, clipped_high_pct/clipped_low_pct (byte>=253 / <=2), wb_ratio_rg/bg (R/G, B/G channel means), sharpness (mean abs horizontal green-channel gradient, monotone within a frame only), downscale (nearest-neighbour stride decimation).
existing_infra.xmp_snapshot: run_editor_benchmark.py:snapshot_xmp / compact_snapshot decode the darktable XMP sidecar's history stack into per-module params (SNAPSHOT_OPS: exposure, sigmoid, temperature, colorbalancergb, colorzones, lens, sharpen, denoiseprofile) for before/after diffing.
existing_infra.outcome_categories: verified, correct_refusal, over_budget, partial, honest_refusal, reported_ok_unverified, blocked, failed (run_editor_benchmark.py OUTCOMES); scoring is pass/partial/fail per task from assertion groups (scoring.pass / scoring.partial / scoring.refusal).
existing_infra.observed_hang: 20260926t092247z-olympus.md: all 27 tasks scored blocked because the first history_commit after darktable launch returned error:commit_timeout in every one of 4 sessions -- this is the exact hang class item H1 below, caught live by the existing harness, not hypothetical.

metrics.how: Snapshot the XMP before and after the call (snapshot_xmp), diff module param values per SNAPSHOT_OPS, assert delta/direction/restored against the task's expected value with a tolerance.
metrics.tolerance_guidance: Exact equality for boolean/enable flags; small absolute tolerance (e.g. +/-0.02 stops on exposure, +/-50K on temperature) for float params, since darktable's own UI step granularity sets the floor -- pick the tolerance from the module's UI step, not an arbitrary epsilon.

metrics.what: Luminance / exposure statistics on exported preview
metrics.how: darktable-cli export to PPM at a fixed long edge (512px matches existing clip_scan usage), run ppm.stats: luminance_mean, luminance_p01/p50/p99, per-channel clipped_high_pct/clipped_low_pct.
metrics.tolerance_guidance: Convert 8-bit luma to EV or L* before comparing across exposure changes (EV delta = log2(new_mean/old_mean); L* = 116*(Y/Yn)^{1/3}-16 for Y>0.008856): a +1 stop instruction should show roughly +1 EV in mean luminance, not a fixed byte-count tolerance, because response is nonlinear near clipping.

metrics.how: Compare clipped_high_pct/clipped_low_pct and luminance_p01/p99 before vs after against the sentence's intent (e.g. 'pull highlights back' should reduce clipped_high_pct, not raise it).
metrics.tolerance_guidance: Direction-only assertion (delta sign) is more robust than an absolute target for 'a touch'/'a lot' style instructions; reserve absolute percent thresholds for chart-based calibration tasks (see M6).

metrics.what: RGB means and colour cast via grey-world
metrics.how: Grey-world assumption: average scene reflectance is neutral, so channel means R:G:B should be near 1:1:1 after a correct white-balance edit; ppm.stats already reports wb_ratio_rg/wb_ratio_bg for this.
metrics.tolerance_guidance: Grey-world is a heuristic, not ground truth, for any scene with a dominant colour (foliage, skin-heavy portrait) -- use it only on the neutral test chart (M8) for absolute cast checks; on real photos use it only for direction (warmer/cooler moved the ratio the expected way).

metrics.what: Chroma/saturation in a perceptual space; hue angle of skin/sky/foliage regions
metrics.how: Convert RGB (as read from PPM) to CIELAB or a simple HSL/HSV approximation with stdlib math (no numpy needed: matrix-multiply RGB->XYZ->Lab per pixel or per sampled block); compute chroma C*=sqrt(a*^2+b*^2) and hue angle atan2(b*,a*); sample fixed regions (top third = sky, centre = subject/skin, edges = foliage where the test frame has it) rather than whole-image means, since whole-image hue is meaningless.
metrics.tolerance_guidance: Hue angle tolerance ~+/-5 deg for 'shift greens toward yellow' style tasks; chroma delta as a percentage of the pre-edit chroma, since absolute chroma varies hugely by scene.

metrics.how: Compute L* histogram from the PPM (via the RGB->Lab conversion in M5) and take a spread statistic: IQR (p75-p25) or std-dev of L*.
metrics.tolerance_guidance: 'Add contrast' should increase L* spread and steepen the midtone slope; assert delta sign plus a minimum magnitude (e.g. >=2 L* units) to reject no-op passes.

metrics.how: High-frequency energy in a flat region: variance of pixel values in a patch expected to be smooth (sky, shadow), or a simple wavelet/Laplacian high-pass proxy computed with the same stdlib gradient technique as ppm.sharpness but on a flat crop instead of the whole frame.
metrics.tolerance_guidance: Denoise tasks should show a measurable decrease (e.g. >=15%) in this patch variance without a corresponding drop in the sharpness metric elsewhere in the frame (to catch over-smoothing false positives).

metrics.how: ppm.py:sharpness already implements a horizontal-gradient proxy (mean abs green-channel diff, sampled every 4th row); a true discrete Laplacian (2D second-derivative kernel) is a small stdlib addition (3x3 convolution over the green channel, no numpy) and is closer to the classic 'variance of Laplacian' focus-measure used in autofocus/blur-detection literature.
metrics.tolerance_guidance: Only compare within the same frame/crop (explicitly documented as scene-relative, not cross-scene, in ppm.py's own docstring); sharpen tasks should raise it, denoise tasks should not crash it to near zero.

metrics.what: Colour cast via ΔE2000 on a grey ramp / colour checker rendered synthetically
metrics.how: Generate a synthetic 'RAW-equivalent' test chart (see M10) with a neutral grey ramp (5-9 patches, L* stepped 10-90, a*=b*=0) and/or a MacBeth-style colour-checker layout with known Lab targets; after an edit, sample each patch's mean Lab from the exported PPM and compute CIEDE2000 against the known target using the Sharma/Wu/Dalal 2005 reference formula (Rochester ECE implementation notes, http://www.ece.rochester.edu/~gsharma/ciede2000/, and https://hajim.rochester.edu/ece/sites/gsharma/papers/CIEDE2000CRNAFeb05.pdf, both 2005, still the standard reference as of 2026). Implement in pure Python: XYZ->Lab is closed-form; CIEDE2000 is ~40 lines of arithmetic, no dependency needed.
metrics.tolerance_guidance: darktable's own integration test suite (darktable-org/darktable-tests, README, accessed 2026-09) passes a rendered frame against a reference PNG when max ΔE < 2.3 and mean ΔE < 2.3/3 across the whole image -- use the same threshold family for a per-patch chart check: pass at ΔE00<2.3, flag at 2.3-5 as a look drift, fail above 5.

metrics.what: Building a synthetic test chart for stable look assertions
metrics.how: Two options: (a) a neutral test frame -- shoot or keep on file one real RAW of a grey card / X-Rite ColorChecker under controlled light, imported into the bench library once, so 'target Lab per patch' is measured, not assumed; (b) a fully synthetic PPM/TIFF chart generated in Python (flat colour blocks at known sRGB values, converted to camera-native via a known matrix) fed through darktable-cli with a neutral (all-defaults) history stack to get a stable baseline render. Prefer (a) for realism (matches what the camera's demosaic/CFA actually does) and (b) only for pure-pipeline unit tests that don't touch a real sensor.
inputs: ColorChecker RAW frame (recommended) or synthetic RGB chart
metrics.tolerance_guidance: Re-render the untouched chart on every darktable/scouter version bump and diff against the last known-good render (ΔE00 per patch) before trusting any look assertion that version -- this catches darktable itself changing its default pipeline output, which would otherwise look like a scouter regression.

properties.statement: Idempotence of repeat: applying the same absolute-magnitude edit twice in a row leaves the sidecar params unchanged after the second call (module already at that value); applying the same relative edit twice roughly doubles the delta (within tolerance), it does not no-op.

Commutativity where expected: independent-axis edits (e.g. white balance temperature then exposure) produce the same final XMP params regardless of call order; edits on the same axis or with known pipeline-order dependence (e.g. lens correction before/after crop) are NOT expected to commute -- assert non-commutativity explicitly there so a false 'pass' isn't hiding a real pipeline-order bug.
properties.applies_to: any two darkroom_set/darkroom_say calls on independent modules

properties.statement: Undo inverts: darkroom_undo_last after a set/adjust restores the pre-call XMP param value (or removes the just-added history entry) within the same tolerance as the original assertion.
properties.applies_to: darkroom_undo_last -- flagged in the vault's 2026-09-24 editor-benchmark note as currently NOT holding over MCP (each call gets its own job, so the undo journal is empty and it still reports ok:true with outcome dry_run); this property is the regression test to re-run once that's fixed.

properties.statement: Monotonic response to magnitude words: for the same module/param, the measured delta for 'a touch' < 'a bit' < 'a lot' < 'a full stop' (or the module's equivalent phrase ladder), strictly increasing in magnitude even if not linear.
properties.applies_to: darkroom_say phrase resolution (the $hist/$ref-style resolvers already used for plan v2 magnitude pinning per editor_tasks.json plan_versions note)

properties.statement: Metamorphic: brighten(x) then darken(same amount) returns to within tolerance of the original export's luminance stats (M2); this validates the round-trip without needing to know the 'correct' absolute value, only the relation.
Metamorphic: a crop/rotate/lens-correction-only edit should not move the grey-world channel ratios (M4) or the luminance histogram (M2) on a neutral chart -- geometric ops should be colour-neutral.

Golden-image regression: the untouched neutral chart (M10) re-rendered through darktable-cli with the checked-in default history must match the last committed reference PPM/stats within ΔE00<2.3 (same threshold family as darktable's own integration suite) -- a mismatch means darktable itself changed, not scouter, and should block the release until re-baselined.
properties.applies_to: chart baseline render, run once per darktable version

hang_causes.cause: Lua/bridge calls executed off the GTK main thread touching GUI state without the darktable gui_lock, or vice versa (GUI callbacks writing state that pixelpipe worker threads read unsynchronized)
hang_causes.evidence: darktable-org/darktable GitHub, 2026: issue #22064 'IOP mask display toggles shared without locking', issue #22133 'toneequal: scrolled() takes gui_lock then history_mutex, deadlocking the darkroom' (AB-BA lock-order inversion), PR #21912 'dev-doc: document sharing gui_data between GUI and pipe threads' (introduces GUI_Threading.md), PR #22365 'Fixing unsafe read&write of g->data'. All accessed 2026-09-26.
hang_causes.mitigation: Never call darktable.gui.action or any widget-touching Lua from a background thread; serialize all scouter bridge calls through darktable's own idle/GTK callback mechanism; treat any call that touches GUI + pixelpipe state together as a known deadlock risk and prefer the non-GUI Lua API / darktable-cli path where one exists.

hang_causes.cause: Modal dialogs blocking the GTK main loop (any Lua/bridge call issued while a dialog is open never gets processed)
hang_causes.evidence: General GTK single-threaded-main-loop behaviour plus the same darktable threading issues above; also matches the harness's own observed pattern where the first history_commit after launch hung in every 2026-09-26 session (see existing_infra.observed_hang) -- consistent with an unacknowledged dialog or first-commit UI state not yet settled.
hang_causes.mitigation: Health-check (ping) before every state-changing call; if a dialog-class hang is suspected, send Escape/dismiss via the same bridge before retrying; add a settle delay after launch before the first history_commit (the harness already waits ~2-2.4s for 'ready' per the results markdown, but that is launch-readiness, not first-commit-readiness -- these may need separate settle windows).

hang_causes.cause: Pixelpipe (image processing pipeline) blocking the thread issuing the Lua call while a full-res recompute is in flight
hang_causes.evidence: darktable-org/darktable issue #22133 above describes exactly a pixelpipe/history_mutex interaction that can freeze the darkroom with no redraw or input possible; general darktable architecture (pixelpipe runs on worker threads, GUI thread must not block waiting on it under a shared lock).
hang_causes.mitigation: Poll with a bounded timeout rather than a blocking wait; on timeout, treat the call as failed-but-retryable-after-relaunch, not as a fatal crash; avoid firing multiple state-changing calls in quick succession without waiting for pixeline settle.

hang_causes.cause: macOS-specific GTK quirks (window/attention-request spam, view bouncing) adding a source of nondeterministic timing on macOS specifically
hang_causes.evidence: darktable-org/darktable PR #21949 'gui: keep background jobs on GTK thread and avoid Windows attention spam' shows platform-specific GTK behaviour differences are an active area of fixes in 2026 (Windows-flagged in that PR title, but it demonstrates the general pattern of platform GTK quirks affecting responsiveness); darktable-tests PR #43 'Integration tests can now run on macOS' (darktable-org/darktable-tests, accessed 2026-09-26) shows macOS support for the test harness itself was only recently added, implying macOS timing/behaviour was not the original baseline.
hang_causes.mitigation: Fewer view bounces: avoid rapid darkroom<->lighttable switches in a single session; run one darktable process per job with a dedicated --library and --configdir so no shared state carries hang-inducing history between jobs; add a watchdog that SIGKILLs and relaunches darktable after N seconds of no bridge response (the harness's results markdown already shows 'quit SIGKILL' as the fallback path when quit hangs).

steps: Create isolated HOME/XDG dirs for the rehearsal, e.g. a scratch root under ~/Pictures/ScouterScratch/install-rehearsal/<stamp>/ with its own home/, config/, cache/ subfolders -- never point at the real $HOME.

Set HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME (and darktable's own --configdir flag) to the scratch subfolders for every subprocess in the rehearsal, mirroring acceptance_driver.py's pattern of overriding SCOUTER_CONFIG/SCOUTER_CACHE/OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH per env in acc_env()/base_env().

Launch darktable once against the throwaway --configdir to let it generate a fresh darktablerc, library.db and luarc under the scratch config dir -- confirms first-run config generation works, not just steady-state operation.

Run `scouter setup` against SCOUTER_CONFIG pointed at the scratch config path; verify it writes a valid config.json (schema/version field present) without touching ~/.config/darktable or the real scouter config.
Run `scouter setup --check` and assert it reports healthy against the throwaway darktable configdir, catching any assumption the code makes about a pre-existing real install.

Verify MCP registration in Claude Code: check the MCP server entry (claude mcp list / the project's .mcp.json or user-level MCP config) points at `python -m scouter.mcp.server` with the rehearsal's env vars scoped correctly, so a fresh machine's Claude Code would pick up the right binary path and env without inheriting the developer machine's real config.
Tear down: delete the scratch root; confirm nothing was written outside it by diffing `find ~/.config/darktable ~/Library/Application\ Support -newer <rehearsal-start-timestamp>` before/after.
Repeat once with a pre-existing but empty real-looking config (simulating 'user ran setup once before, now re-runs it') to check setup is idempotent, not just clean-slate safe.

report_sections.title: Headline
report_sections.content: One line: N tasks, pass/partial/fail counts and percentage, crash count, run duration, git commit/branch -- the run_editor_benchmark.py markdown header (see results/20260926t092247z-olympus.md line 6) is already close to this shape.

report_sections.title: Per-category pass rates
report_sections.content: Table: category x {pass, partial, fail, score%} -- already produced by summarise()/markdown() in run_editor_benchmark.py; keep it in the release report unchanged.

report_sections.title: Every failure with a repro command
report_sections.content: For each non-pass task: id, sentence, plan calls, outcome label, and a single copy-pasteable repro (e.g. the exact --live --task-id invocation or the MCP call sequence with arguments) so a human can reproduce without reading code.

report_sections.title: Contact sheet of looks
report_sections.content: A single image grid (thumbnail per task: before crop | after crop, or before/after full frame downscaled) so a human can eyeball whether 'passing' edits actually look right -- deterministic metrics can pass on a technically-correct-but-ugly edit, so this is the human sanity check the numbers can't replace.

report_sections.title: Timing percentiles
report_sections.content: p50/p90/p99 wall time per call type (darkroom_set, darkroom_say, history_commit, export_run, etc.) and per whole-task budget, flagging over_budget outcomes distinctly from fail.

report_sections.title: Crash count
report_sections.content: Count of new entries under ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports matching darktable since the run started (acceptance_driver.py:crash_count already implements this) plus any bridge_timeout/blocked session count as a near-crash signal.

report_sections.title: Honest refusals as the roadmap
report_sections.content: The full list of honest_refusal and correct_refusal outcomes with their sentences (e.g. U1/U2 'mask and lift her face', 'remove the person' from the Olympus results) presented not as failures but as the literal backlog of capabilities to build next -- this reframing is what lets a human sign off in 10 minutes: refusals are expected and roadmap-worthy, only reported_ok_unverified and failed are true release blockers.

report_sections.title: Sign-off checklist
report_sections.content: A single yes/no block at the top: zero reported_ok_unverified outcomes, zero unexplained blocked sessions, crash count 0, contact sheet reviewed, all fail-category repro commands present -- gate release on this block, everything else is supporting detail.
